newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares ends weekly trade buoyant.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares ends weekly trade buoyant.

text.p: Jordanian stocks closed firmer at end of weekly trade on Wednesday led by a year-end buying spree by the state pension fund in improved investor confidence over prospects of trade ties with Iraq.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.05 percent to 153.70 points, hitting nine-month highs for the third time in a week, on busy turnover worth 1.52 million dinars ($2.14 million).

Brokers said activity was dominated by continued end-of- year buying by the cash-rich state pension fund, Jordan Social Security corporation, focusing on selected industrials with Jordan Cement and Jordan Electric Power topping the list of favourites.

Investor sentiment has been buoyed by opportunities arising from Iraq's near implemetation of its oil-for food deal that the business community hopes could activate stagnant industrial sectors and improve next year's performance of blue-chip firms exporting to Iraq.
Key industrials Jordan Cement Factories and Jordan Electric rose 0.07 dinars to 3.56 dinars with continued brisk demand, brokers said .
Drug firm Arab Pharmaceutical Chemicals, rising 0.06 dinars to 1.54 dinars, dominated turnover with 153,878 dinars of stock exchanging hands.
Overall 10 stocks rose while 20 declined. Another 15 traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of 45 best-traded shares fell 0.06 percent to 82.53, still 13.59 percent down on last year.
